# Exit codes

<!-- Generated by bin/exit-codes.mjs — do not hand-edit; run `node bin/exit-codes.mjs` to refresh. -->

Each table is what the command's header comment declares, read by `bin/exit-codes.mjs`. It is not
verified against the code paths that set the exit status. `undeclared` means the header says
nothing about exit status; `prose` means it does, in a shape the extractor does not tabulate.
Neither is a claim about what the command returns. What may change between releases is in
[STABILITY.md](STABILITY.md).

306 commands: 112 declared, 12 prose, 182 undeclared. Of the declared, 100 use only codes 0–13, the range Node itself exits with (1 on an uncaught exception), and 12 declare a code of 20 or above.

## `commitwork` subcommands

### `commitwork init`

Declared in `bin/init.mjs` (`runInit`).

| Exit | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| 0 | ready |
| 1 | refused (existing state init would not have created) |
| 2 | usage |

Undeclared: `list`, `run`, `scan`, `brief`, `sarif`, `reindex`, `doctor`, `setup`, `hook`, `help`.

| 0 | nothing flagged, nothing unclassified, no open finding |
| 21 | at least one row flagged |
| 2 | the sweep itself failed to run (an unreadable closure point is not a clean loop) |
| 23 | nothing flagged or unclassified but at least one named open finding |
| 24 | nothing flagged but at least one row UNCLASSIFIED: a warning that a closure point went unchecked, printed with a suggested fix where one can be derived. 21 beats 24 beats 23: a flag is the strongest statement, and a point nobody checked outranks a gap already named. Every count still travels in the report. |
